correctness.rationale: Full ar5iv HTML source arXiv:1801.02785 Theorem 9 lines 359–365 DOES state 0≤lambda1,lambda2<1/2 and arbitrary mu>0 for the exact weighted quadratic inequality. Explicit one-index H=C,K=I,W=H,V=0,w=a=b=1,lambda1=lambda2=0,mu=1 satisfies it but yields Y=0, disproving the published conclusion. For correction, weighted direct-sum analysis norms X,Y,D obey X²≥Aa_-²||K*f||² and D²≤pX²+qY² with p=lambda1+mu/(Aa_-²),q=lambda2. Reverse-triangle bounds |X−Y|≤D, and for X>0 r=Y/X lies between r±=(1±sqrt(p+q−pq))/(1−q); p<1 ensures positive r_- and q<1. Direct coefficient confinement converts to the displayed K-fusion bounds Aa_-²r_-²/b_+² and Ba_+²r_+²/b_-². For X=0, K*f=0; upper bound still follows D≤sqrt(q)Y then triangle. The boundary/supercritical one-index construction makes Y=0 whenever mu≥(1−lambda1)Aa_-², proving sharp UNIVERSAL sufficiency, not individual-family failure. Independently checked quadratic root identity and direct counterexample, not relying on finite stress logs.
